_doc: PARKER dating cabinet (#18, built 2026-07-17). The Dunhill second WITH ITS OWN DATE CODE — three documented regimes, encoded as a generic code_table (engine growth 2026-07-17, brand-agnostic lookup): 1923 = NO code; 1924-1942 = consecutive 1..19 (year = 1923+n); WWII gap (Parker not government-approved — made the bakelite/clay 'Wunup' instead; ONE known 19-code 1942 briar, Jason Lynn photos); 1945-1949 = codes 20..24; 1950-1957 = UNDERLINED RAISED 0..7 (record as 'u0'..'u7'); after 1957 codes AND patent numbers cease. The code always follows 'MADE IN LONDON over ENGLAND'. SOURCES (local-first): staging/pipedia/Parker.json (incl. Loring 'The Dunhill Briar Pipe' + the John Campbell/ASP letter + dated exemplars: Super Briar Bark 73/F pat.116989/17 code 14 = 1937; underlined-5 = 1955). ⚠️ PERCEPTION RULE: a bare digit 1-7 maps to the 1920s per the table; if the digit is UNDERLINED/RAISED it must be recorded as 'u<digit>' (1950s). Loring caveat: very few Parkers are true Dunhill 'failings' (most graded out pre-finishing; briar also bought elsewhere) — never claim Dunhill production without provenance.

history_anchors._doc: 1922 Parker Pipe Co Ltd formed by Alfred Dunhill to finish and market Dunhill 'failings' (before that: X-overstamp or 'Damaged Price' on Dunhill's own). 1923 first Parker pipes (no date code year). 1935 Dunhill opens a factory next door to Hardcastle; 1936 buys 49% of Hardcastle (some non-possessive PARKER stamps from 1936); 1946 buys the rest; 1967 PARKER-HARDCASTLE LIMITED formed -> from 1967 the brand is fully independent product-wise (never sold in Dunhill's own catalogues/stores). US market: strong 1930s-1950s, faded, RE-INTRODUCED 1991. WWII: 'Wunup' bakelite+clay pipe. Patent stamped up to 1954 = the Inner-Tube-with-flange patent.

brand_marks.physical: Date code follows the circular MADE IN LONDON over straight ENGLAND stamp. 'F' suffix on shapes = likely Fantail (as on Dunhill). Possessive PARKER'S = pre-WWII usage (non-possessive existed from at least 1936).

date_code._doc: code_table regimes: '1'..'19' = 1923+n (1924-1942); '20'..'24' = 1945-1949 (post-war restart, 1943-44 skipped); 'u0'..'u7' = underlined raised digits 1950-1957. No code + pre-war profile could be 1923 (or worn) -> confirm-flow, never guessed. Codes end 1957.

table.note: the Inner-Tube-with-flange patent; patent numbers stamped only up to 1954 (dated exemplar: code 14 = 1937 Super Briar Bark)
the standard Parker origin stamp from the start -> brand floor only; the DATE CODE after it does the precise work (absent after 1957)

line_years._notes: wunup: the WWII bakelite+clay pipe (Parker wasn't an approved wartime briar manufacturer) -> war-years bracket. NOT encoded: super briar bark / super bruyere bark (single dated exemplars 1937/1955 — the date CODE dates them), select (undated estate name).

table.label: possessive PARKER'S stamp = pre-WWII usage (non-possessive existed from at least 1936 -> overlap; wide honest end 1941)

channels_future.post_1957: After 1957: no codes, no patents -> post-57 Parkers date only by line/catalogue evidence (1958 pamphlet + Parker-Hardcastle brochures are pictured on pipedia — mirror + mine for line brackets). Pipedia itself asks for post-1957 code info — none documented.
channels_future.us_reintro: US re-introduction 1991 -> a US-market-only line name could gain a 1991 floor if catalogues land.
channels_future.shape_letters: 'F' = Fantail (as Dunhill). Shape-number reader already proven on the Parker '575' class (see method notes).

_note_alias_qc_2026_07_17: QC fix: alias 'parker-hardcastle' removed here — hardcastle.json owns it (deterministic routing; its era ladder closes on the 1967 Parker-Hardcastle merger). A pipe stamped only 'Parker-Hardcastle' routes to hardcastle; Parker-stamped pipes stay here.
